neck.title: Neck lump: from site to diagnosis
neck.source: NICE NG12 & NG36 · UK Head & Neck MDT 2016 · Bailey & Love 28e

nodes.t: Patient with a lump in the neck
History: age, duration, smoking, alcohol, B symptoms · site, movement, transillumination, pulsatility + **full ENT exam with nasendoscopy**

n.t: Moves up on **tongue protrusion** → **thyroglossal cyst**: USS (confirm normal thyroid) → **Sistrunk’s operation** (cyst + tract + central hyoid)
Moves on swallowing only → thyroid (nodule pathway) · submental, not moving → dermoid cyst → excision
Anterior to upper third of SCM → **branchial cyst**: USS ± FNA (cholesterol crystals) → complete excision once infection settles
Soft, transilluminant, posterior triangle in infant → **lymphatic malformation**: MRI → **sclerotherapy** (OK-432, bleomycin) or excision
**Carotid body paraganglioma**: moves side to side, not vertically · **never FNA or biopsy**
CT/MR angiography (splayed ICA/ECA – lyre sign), plasma metanephrines, SDHx gene testing
Excision by vascular/H&N team (Shamblin grade predicts risk) or surveillance/radiotherapy if elderly or unfit
Recent URTI, tender → reactive: treat and **review at 3–6 weeks**; persisting node → sample (below)

nodes.t: Persistent unexplained neck lump (esp. age ≥ 45, smoker) or cystic lateral mass > 40 y → **2-week-wait head & neck referral**
**USS-guided FNA/core biopsy** first · CT/MRI neck + chest · never open excision of a possible SCC node

n.t: p16/HPV, **PET-CT**, panendoscopy ± tonsillectomy/tongue-base mucosectomy for unknown primary → H&N MDT
Core or **excision biopsy** for architecture → haematology (staging PET-CT)
AFB smear, culture, GeneXpert → **6-month anti-TB therapy**; aspirate cold abscess, avoid incision (sinus)

nodes.t: Adult cystic lateral neck mass = metastatic (HPV+ oropharyngeal) SCC until proven otherwise

neck.title: Thyroid nodule and goitre
neck.source: BTA 2014 thyroid cancer · NICE NG145 (2019) & NG230 (2022)

nodes.t: Thyroid nodule or goitre (palpable or incidental)
**TSH first** · low TSH → isotope scan: hot nodule = toxic adenoma (rarely malignant) → treat hyperthyroidism, no FNA
Red flags: rapid growth, stridor, hoarseness, fixed hard mass, nodes, childhood neck irradiation, MEN2 family history → urgent referral
**Ultrasound U-score**: U1 normal · U2 benign · U3 indeterminate · U4 suspicious · U5 malignant → **USS-guided FNA if U3–U5**

n.t: **Repeat USS-guided FNA** (± core); Thy1c cyst with benign USS → observe
Reassure/discharge if U2 · repeat FNA if U3–U5 or clinical concern
Thy3a → repeat FNA/core, MDT · Thy3f & Thy4 → **diagnostic hemithyroidectomy**
Stage (USS nodes ± CT) → MDT → definitive surgery by tumour type (below)
≤ 4 cm, N0, low risk → **hemithyroidectomy** · > 4 cm, extrathyroidal, nodes or metastases → **total thyroidectomy** ± neck dissection
Risk-adapted **radioiodine** + TSH suppression for high risk; follow-up with thyroglobulin
Calcitonin, CEA, **RET testing** · **exclude phaeochromocytoma first**
**Total thyroidectomy + central neck dissection**; no role for radioiodine
Anaplastic: secure airway, BRAF testing, MDT (usually palliative) · lymphoma (Hashimoto’s): core biopsy → **R-CHOP ± RT**, not surgery

nodes.t: Benign nodular goitre: **no thyroxine suppression** · surgery only for compression, retrosternal extension, growth or cosmesis

neck.title: Thyrotoxicosis and safe thyroidectomy
neck.source: NICE NG145 (2019) · ETA 2018 Graves · DAS/BAETS 2022 haematoma

nodes.t: Low TSH with raised FT4/FT3: tremor, palpitations, weight loss, heat intolerance
**Propranolol** for symptoms (diltiazem if asthmatic) · TSH-receptor antibodies (TRAb) · isotope scan if TRAb negative or nodular

n.t: **Carbimazole** 12–18 months (titration or block-and-replace); PTU in 1st trimester
Warn: sore throat/fever → urgent FBC (**agranulocytosis**) · relapse ~50% → definitive treatment
Antithyroid drug to euthyroid → **radioiodine** or surgery (hemithyroidectomy / total) – rarely remits
Painful, post-partum or amiodarone: beta-blocker ± NSAID/steroid; **no antithyroid drugs**

nodes.t: Definitive: **radioiodine** (not in pregnancy, avoid conception 6 months, steroid cover/avoid if active orbitopathy) or **total thyroidectomy**
Surgery if compressive goitre, active eye disease, suspicious nodule, pregnancy plans or choice · pre-op euthyroid + **potassium iodide 10 days**
Pre-op laryngoscopy (cords), calcium · post-op levothyroxine, **adjusted Ca/PTH next morning**

n.t: **SCOOP at bedside**: Skin exposure, Cut sutures, Open skin, Open muscles, Pack → then theatre; call anaesthetist
Mild: oral calcium + **alfacalcidol** · tetany/QT long: **10 mL 10% calcium gluconate IV** over 10 min, then infusion
Unilateral RLN palsy → laryngoscopy, voice therapy · bilateral → **reintubation / tracheostomy**
**Thyroid storm**: ICU, propranolol, PTU then iodide 1 h later, hydrocortisone, cooling, fluids

nodes.t: Make the patient euthyroid before any surgery or radioiodine – prevents thyroid storm

endo.title: Hypercalcaemia and hyperparathyroidism
endo.source: NICE NG132 (2019) · 5th International Workshop PHPT 2022 · KDIGO 2017 CKD-MBD

nodes.t: Raised albumin-adjusted calcium (often incidental): stones, bones, groans, psychic moans
Ca > 3.0 mmol/L or symptomatic → **IV 0.9% saline 3–4 L/24 h**, then IV bisphosphonate (zoledronate); stop thiazides
Repeat adjusted Ca + **PTH**, phosphate, 25-OH vitamin D, eGFR

n.t: Non-parathyroid: **malignancy** (PTHrP, myeloma screen), vitamin D excess, sarcoid, drugs → treat cause
**Primary HPT** (solitary adenoma ~85%) · exclude **FHH**: urine Ca:Cr clearance ratio < 0.01 → no surgery
**Secondary HPT**: phosphate restriction + binders, vitamin D, alfacalcidol, **cinacalcet** → parathyroidectomy if refractory

br.l: High Ca after long CKD / transplant

n.t: **Tertiary HPT** (autonomous): cinacalcet → **subtotal (3½-gland) or total parathyroidectomy + forearm autograft**

nodes.t: Primary HPT: replete vitamin D · renal USS (stones), DEXA incl. distal radius, 24-h urine calcium
Surgery if symptoms, renal stones, osteoporosis/fragility fracture, eGFR < 60 or **adjusted Ca ≥ 2.85 mmol/L** (consider in all)

n.t: Localise: **neck USS + sestamibi SPECT-CT** (or 4D-CT / choline PET)
Concordant → **focused parathyroidectomy** + intra-op PTH (> 50% fall) · non-localised, multigland, MEN → bilateral neck exploration
Monitor Ca & eGFR, DEXA · **cinacalcet** for hypercalcaemia, bisphosphonate for bone; offer surgery again if criteria met

nodes.t: Post-op: watch for **hungry bone syndrome** (calcium + alfacalcidol) · cure = normocalcaemia at 6 months

endo.title: Multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN)
endo.source: ATA 2015 medullary thyroid cancer · Thakker 2012 MEN1 · Bailey & Love 28e

nodes.t: Two or more endocrine tumours, multigland/young HPT, medullary thyroid cancer or family history
Screen: adjusted Ca + PTH, calcitonin, **plasma metanephrines**, prolactin, fasting gut hormones
**Genetic testing**: MEN1 (menin) or **RET proto-oncogene** → cascade-test first-degree relatives

n.t: **Parathyroid hyperplasia** (~95%) → subtotal (3½-gland) or total parathyroidectomy + autotransplant + **transcervical thymectomy**
**Pancreatic NETs** (gastrinoma, insulinoma, non-functioning) → resect if functioning or > 2 cm
**Pituitary** adenoma: prolactinoma → cabergoline; others → trans-sphenoidal surgery
Lifelong annual biochemistry + periodic imaging from childhood
**Exclude phaeochromocytoma first** (plasma metanephrines) → α-blockade → adrenalectomy before other surgery
**Prophylactic total thyroidectomy** by RET risk: high risk (codon 634) **by age 5**; moderate risk when calcitonin rises
Established MTC → total thyroidectomy + central neck dissection; follow calcitonin & CEA
MTC + phaeo + **marfanoid habitus, mucosal neuromas**, no HPT
**Total thyroidectomy in the first year of life** (most aggressive MTC)

nodes.t: Always treat a phaeochromocytoma before thyroid or parathyroid surgery; MTC does not take up radioiodine
Suspected hormone-secreting pancreatic NET

n.t: **Supervised 72-h fast**: glucose < 3.0 mmol/L with raised insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin; negative sulfonylurea screen
Usually single, benign, < 2 cm → **EUS** + CT/MRI (GLP-1R PET if occult) → **enucleation** or distal pancreatectomy
Refractory/multiple/jejunal ulcers + diarrhoea → **fasting gastrin > 10× ULN with gastric pH < 2** (± secretin test)
**High-dose PPI** · gastrinoma triangle (duodenum) · 20–25% MEN1 → resect if sporadic and localised
Glucagonoma: necrolytic migratory erythema, diabetes, DVT · VIPoma: watery diarrhoea, ↓K⁺ → **somatostatin analogue** + resection

nodes.t: Stage: CT/MRI + EUS · **⁶⁸Ga-DOTATATE PET-CT** · grade by Ki-67 (G1 < 3%, G2 3–20%, G3 > 20%)
Screen for MEN1: calcium, PTH, prolactin
Metastatic: somatostatin analogue, **PRRT (¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE)**, everolimus/sunitinib, liver-directed therapy · resect where feasible

bbreast.title: Breast lump: triple assessment
bbreast.source: NICE NG12 · ABS 2019 best-practice diagnostic guidelines · Bailey & Love 28e

nodes.t: Woman with a breast lump
**2-week-wait** if ≥ 30 y with unexplained lump (or skin change, ≥ 50 with nipple change) · < 30 y → non-urgent breast clinic
**Triple assessment** in one-stop clinic: clinical exam + imaging + **core biopsy**
Imaging: **USS if < 40 y**; mammography + USS if ≥ 40 y · score P/U/M 1–5; any score ≥ 3 → core biopsy

n.t: U2 and < 25 y → no biopsy needed · otherwise core-confirm → reassure · > 3 cm, growing or symptomatic → **vacuum-assisted or surgical excision**
**Aspirate** if symptomatic · discard clear fluid · **bloody aspirate or residual mass → core biopsy**
**Phyllodes tumour** on core → **wide local excision with clear margins** (≥ 1 cm if borderline/malignant), no axillary surgery
**Fat necrosis** (oil cyst, coarse calcification) – mimics cancer → core biopsy to confirm

nodes.t: Concordant benign triple assessment → reassure and discharge · any discordance → repeat biopsy or excision
Nipple discharge
Character: one or many ducts, uni/bilateral, spontaneous vs expressed, colour, blood (dipstick), associated lump

n.t: Pregnancy test, **prolactin**, TFT, drug history (antipsychotics, metoclopramide) → pituitary MRI if prolactin high
Physiological / **duct ectasia** (smokers, perimenopause) → imaging if ≥ 40 y → reassure
**Mammography + USS** (≥ 40 y) or USS (< 40) ± core biopsy of any lesion
Commonest cause **intraductal papilloma** → **microdochectomy** (diagnostic + therapeutic)

nodes.t: ≥ 50 y with discharge, retraction or other nipple change → **2-week-wait**
Older woman, multiduct troublesome discharge or ectasia → **total duct excision (Hadfield’s)** · eczematous nipple → exclude Paget’s

bbreast.title: Breast pain and breast infection
bbreast.source: NICE CKS 2023 mastitis & mastalgia · ABS 2019 · Bailey & Love 28e

nodes.t: Painful or inflamed breast
Ask: cycle relation, lactation, smoking, drugs (HRT, OCP), trauma · examine for lump, abscess, skin change

n.t: Examine; imaging only if focal lump or signs · pain alone is **not** a cancer red flag
**Reassurance**, well-fitting bra, **topical NSAID**; pain diary · evening primrose oil not recommended
Severe refractory: specialist tamoxifen 10 mg (off-label) · danazol rarely (side-effects)
**Continue breastfeeding/expressing**, analgesia · **flucloxacillin** 10–14 days (clarithromycin if penicillin allergy)
Fluctuant/not settling → USS → **needle aspiration** (repeat) or mini-incision drainage
Young smoker, periareolar → **co-amoxiclav** (or clarithromycin + metronidazole), **stop smoking**
Abscess → USS-guided aspiration · recurrent or **mammary duct fistula** → total duct excision + fistula excision

nodes.t: Inflammation not settling after one or two antibiotic courses → imaging + **core/punch biopsy**
Persistent erythema, oedema, peau d’orange despite antibiotics = **inflammatory breast cancer** until proven otherwise

bca.title: Suspected breast cancer: diagnosis and staging
bca.source: NICE NG101 (2018, updated) · NICE NG12 · ESMO 2024 early breast cancer

nodes.t: Breast lump, skin/nipple change, axillary node or screen-detected abnormality
**Triple assessment**: exam + mammography/USS + **core biopsy** → ER, PR, **HER2**, grade, Ki-67
**Axillary USS** ± core/FNA of abnormal node · MRI if lobular, dense breasts, size discordance, Paget’s or occult primary
Staging CT chest/abdomen/pelvis ± bone scan **only** if T3–4, N2–3, inflammatory, symptoms or high-risk neoadjuvant

n.t: **Primary surgery**, or neoadjuvant systemic therapy if HER2+ or triple-negative ≥ T2/N+, or to permit breast conservation
**Neoadjuvant chemotherapy** (+ HER2 therapy) → mastectomy + ALND + chest-wall RT; no immediate reconstruction if inflammatory
Biopsy a metastasis (receptors) → **systemic therapy by subtype**; surgery only for palliation

nodes.t: **Germline BRCA testing** if triple-negative < 60 y, diagnosis < 40 y, male breast cancer, or ≥ 10% carrier probability
Paget’s nipple, male breast lump and inflammatory change are cancer until biopsy proves otherwise

bca.title: Breast and axillary surgery
bca.source: NICE NG101 · ABS 2023 · Z0011 / AMAROS / FAST-Forward trials

nodes.t: Operable invasive breast cancer

n.t: **Wide local excision** (± oncoplastic) with clear margins: no tumour on ink (invasive), ≥ 2 mm (DCIS)
Always + **whole-breast RT 26 Gy in 5 fractions** (may omit if ≥ 65 y, T1N0, ER+, low grade on endocrine)
Large tumour:breast ratio, multicentric, RT contraindicated, inflammatory, BRCA or choice
Offer **immediate reconstruction** (implant or flap) · post-mastectomy RT if N+ or T3–4
**Sentinel lymph node biopsy** (isotope + blue dye, or magnetic tracer)
BCS + RT + systemic therapy → **no further axillary surgery** (Z0011) · mastectomy → axillary RT or ALND
**Axillary node clearance** (levels I–II) or axillary RT; after neoadjuvant response → targeted axillary surgery

nodes.t: DCIS: BCS + RT (or mastectomy if extensive) · SLNB only if mastectomy or suspected invasion
Watch for seroma, lymphoedema, intercostobrachial numbness, **long thoracic (winged scapula)** and thoracodorsal nerve injury

bca.title: Adjuvant systemic therapy by receptor status
bca.source: NICE NG101 · ESMO 2024 early breast cancer · NICE TA810/TA851/TA886

nodes.t: Breast cancer after surgery, or before it (neoadjuvant)
Estimate benefit with **PREDICT** ± gene expression test (Oncotype DX) for ER+/HER2−, node 0–3

n.t: **Endocrine therapy 5–10 years**: premenopausal → tamoxifen (± ovarian suppression + AI if high risk); postmenopausal → **aromatase inhibitor**
Chemotherapy if high genomic/PREDICT risk · **abemaciclib 2 y** if node+ high risk · olaparib if gBRCA
Chemotherapy + **trastuzumab 1 year** (+ pertuzumab if node+) · **baseline + 3-monthly echo** (cardiotoxicity)
Residual disease after neoadjuvant → **T-DM1** (trastuzumab emtansine)
Neoadjuvant anthracycline–taxane + carboplatin + **pembrolizumab** (if ≥ T2 or N+)
Residual disease → **capecitabine** (or olaparib if gBRCA)

nodes.t: Postmenopausal node-positive → **adjuvant bisphosphonate** (zoledronic acid) · AI → DEXA; tamoxifen → VTE & endometrial risk
Metastatic ER+: AI/fulvestrant + **CDK4/6 inhibitor** · HER2+: trastuzumab + pertuzumab + docetaxel · bone mets: denosumab/bisphosphonate

saliv.title: Salivary gland lump (parotid / submandibular)
saliv.source: BAHNO/ENT UK 2020 · NICE NG36 · Bailey & Love 28e

nodes.t: Discrete, persistent lump in the parotid or submandibular region
Examine **facial nerve function**, skin fixation, deep-lobe (parapharyngeal) extension, neck nodes; 80% rule: parotid, benign, pleomorphic
**Ultrasound + US-guided FNAC or core biopsy**; never open/incisional biopsy (seeding, nerve injury)
MRI if deep lobe, malignant cytology or fixed; CT neck/chest for staging malignancy; discuss at head & neck MDT

n.t: **Superficial parotidectomy** or extracapsular dissection with nerve monitoring; submandibular → gland excision
Never enucleate: pseudopod capsule → recurrence; untreated ~5–10% become carcinoma ex-pleomorphic
Older smoker, often bilateral, hot on scintigraphy → **observe** if cytology certain, or excise if symptomatic
**(Total) parotidectomy, preserving the nerve unless involved**; neck dissection if N+ or high grade
Post-op radiotherapy if high grade, close margins, T3–4, perineural invasion · mucoepidermoid commonest, adenoid cystic spreads along nerves

nodes.t: Parotidectomy risks: facial palsy (temporary 20–40%, permanent < 2%), **Frey syndrome** (gustatory sweating), sialocele, earlobe numbness

saliv.title: Painful swelling with meals: stones and sialadenitis

nodes.t: Recurrent gland swelling and pain with eating (salivary colic) ± fever, pus at duct
Exclude dental abscess and reactive lymphadenitis; check hydration, glucose and drugs that dry the mouth
Bimanual palpation of floor of mouth, inspect duct orifice; **ultrasound first line** (sialography/sialendoscopy, CT if needed)

n.t: Dehydrated, elderly, post-op, poor oral hygiene; *Staph. aureus*
**Rehydrate, oral hygiene, sialogogues, massage + IV/oral flucloxacillin or co-amoxiclav**; pus for culture
Abscess on US → aspirate / incise (protect facial nerve)
Distal, palpable stone → **transoral duct incision and removal**
Proximal/hilar → sialendoscopy ± laser or extracorporeal lithotripsy
Intraglandular or recurrent with fibrosis → **submandibular gland excision** (protect marginal mandibular, lingual, hypoglossal nerves)
Mumps: supportive, isolate, check for orchitis/pancreatitis; consider HIV (cysts), sarcoid, Sjögren

nodes.t: Chronic sialadenitis: sialogogues, hydration, massage; sialendoscopy dilatation of strictures; gland excision only if refractory

saliv.title: Other swellings and dry mouth
saliv.source: BSR 2017 Sjögren · ACR/EULAR 2016 criteria · Bailey & Love 28e

nodes.t: Floor-of-mouth/lip cyst, diffuse bilateral enlargement or xerostomia
Bimanual exam, drug history (anticholinergics), alcohol, diabetes, eating disorder; **ultrasound** first-line imaging

n.t: Lower lip after trauma; may resolve → **excise with underlying minor glands** if persistent
**Ranula** (sublingual gland); plunging if through mylohyoid → MRI/US
**Excise the sublingual gland** (± cyst) via mouth; marsupialisation alone recurs
**Sialadenosis**: alcohol, diabetes, malnutrition/bulimia, drugs → treat cause; exclude HIV, sarcoid, lymphoma
**Sjögren**: anti-Ro/La, Schirmer test, labial gland biopsy, US; sialometry
Saliva substitutes, pilocarpine, dental care; watch for **MALT lymphoma** (persistent gland enlargement)

nodes.t: Minor salivary gland lump on palate: majority malignant → biopsy and wide excision

oeso.title: Dysphagia
oeso.source: NICE NG12 · Chicago Classification 4.0 · ESNM/UEG 2020 achalasia

nodes.t: Difficulty swallowing (oesophageal) or choking/coughing on swallow (oropharyngeal)
**Dysphagia at any age = urgent direct-access OGD (2-week wait)** to exclude cancer; biopsy any lesion
OGD normal → biopsies for eosinophils; then barium swallow and **high-resolution manometry**; videofluoroscopy if oropharyngeal

n.t: Absent peristalsis + incomplete LOS relaxation (HRM types I–III); bird’s beak on barium
**Pneumatic dilatation, laparoscopic Heller myotomy + Dor fundoplication or POEM** (POEM best for type III)
Botox if unfit · lifelong ↑ SCC risk
≥ 15 eosinophils/hpf; young atopic man, food bolus, rings/furrows
**PPI, orodispersible budesonide** or elimination diet; dilate strictures; dupilumab if refractory
Elderly, regurgitation, halitosis, gurgling → **endoscopic stapling** or open cricopharyngeal myotomy ± excision
Endoscopic balloon dilatation + long-term PPI

nodes.t: Food bolus obstruction: urgent OGD (within 24 h, < 6 h if total obstruction/drooling); biopsy afterwards to exclude EoE

oeso.title: GORD, hiatus hernia and Barrett’s oesophagus
oeso.source: NICE CG184 · BSG 2014 Barrett’s · ESGE 2023 Barrett’s

nodes.t: Heartburn and regurgitation
Lifestyle: weight loss, stop smoking, raise bed head, avoid late meals; **full-dose PPI for 4–8 weeks**
Alarm features (dysphagia, weight loss, ≥ 55 with symptoms) or refractory → **OGD**

n.t: **24-h pH-impedance off PPI + HRM** (exclude achalasia/ineffective motility)
Laparoscopic **Nissen (or partial) fundoplication** if proven reflux, PPI-responsive or volume regurgitation
Symptomatic → elective repair (risk of gastric volvulus) · acute volvulus: NG decompression, urgent surgery
Surveillance with Seattle biopsies: **< 3 cm 5-yearly, 3–10 cm 3-yearly**; ≥ 10 cm → expert centre
Confirm by 2nd GI pathologist → **endoscopic ablation (RFA)** or 6-monthly surveillance
**Endoscopic resection (EMR/ESD) of visible lesion, then RFA** of residual Barrett’s

nodes.t: Barrett’s: long-term PPI; surveillance only if fit for treatment
Chest pain after vomiting (Boerhaave) or after endoscopy/dilatation; surgical emphysema, fever, shock
Mackler triad: vomiting, chest pain, subcutaneous emphysema; **CT chest/abdomen with oral water-soluble contrast**
**Nil by mouth, IV fluids, broad-spectrum antibiotics + antifungal, IV PPI**, chest drain for effusion, early nutrition (NJ / jejunostomy)

n.t: **Non-operative** (often iatrogenic): close monitoring, repeat contrast study

br.l: Small defect, early, no extensive sepsis

n.t: **Endoscopic**: covered stent, clips or endoluminal vacuum therapy + drainage of collections
**Surgery**: debridement, primary repair (buttressed) + wide drainage
Extensive necrosis or underlying cancer → oesophagectomy or diversion

nodes.t: Mortality doubles if delay > 24 h · caustic ingestion: no induced vomiting, OGD/CT grading within 24 h

stom.title: Dyspepsia, H. pylori and peptic ulcer
stom.source: NICE CG184 · NICE NG12 · Maastricht VI 2022

nodes.t: Upper abdominal pain/discomfort, heartburn, early satiety
Review NSAIDs, aspirin, SSRIs, steroids; check FBC

n.t: **Urgent OGD (2-week wait)**; also upper mass, iron-deficiency anaemia, GI bleeding
**Test-and-treat H. pylori** (stool antigen or 13C-urea breath test; 2 weeks off PPI) **or** full-dose PPI for 1 month
Eradication: PPI + amoxicillin + clarithromycin/metronidazole (NICE 7 days; Maastricht VI 14 days, bismuth quadruple if resistance high)

nodes.t: Peptic ulcer: stop NSAIDs, PPI 8 weeks; confirm eradication with breath test if ulcer
**Gastric ulcer: biopsy and repeat OGD at 6–8 weeks** to confirm healing (exclude cancer) · refractory ulcers → think Zollinger–Ellison (gastrin)
Sudden severe epigastric pain → generalised peritonitis, board-like rigidity
Erect CXR free gas (absent in ~25%) → **CT abdomen** if doubt; lactate, amylase (exclude pancreatitis)
**Resuscitate: IV fluids, NBM, NG tube, IV PPI, broad-spectrum antibiotics** (± antifungal), analgesia, catheter

n.t: **Laparoscopic or open omental patch repair** (Graham) + thorough peritoneal lavage
Biopsy gastric ulcers · large/malignant ulcer → resection
Selected **non-operative (Taylor) regimen**: NG, PPI, antibiotics; operate if no improvement in 12–24 h

nodes.t: Post-op: **eradicate H. pylori**, stop NSAIDs, long-term PPI if NSAID unavoidable · Boey score predicts mortality
Projectile non-bilious vomiting of old food, visible peristalsis, succussion splash, weight loss
Bloods: **hypochloraemic, hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis** with paradoxical aciduria
**NG decompression + IV 0.9% saline with KCl** (correct before surgery); IV PPI
**OGD + biopsy** (after stomach emptied) and CT to stage

n.t: PPI + H. pylori eradication + **endoscopic balloon dilatation**
Failure → antrectomy or gastrojejunostomy
Resectable → staging & curative resection
Palliative: **duodenal stent** (short survival) or gastrojejunostomy / EUS-GE (fitter, longer survival)

nodes.t: After gastric surgery watch for dumping (small frequent dry meals), B12/iron deficiency, bile reflux

intest.title: Intestinal obstruction
intest.source: WSES 2017 ASBO (Bologna) · ESCP/WSES 2021 LBO · Bailey & Love 28e

nodes.t: Colicky pain, vomiting, distension, absolute constipation
**Drip and suck**: IV fluids, NBM, NG tube, catheter; correct K⁺; check hernial orifices, PR, previous surgery
**CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast**: level, cause, closed loop, ischaemia

n.t: Fever, tachycardia, constant pain, ↑ lactate, closed loop, irreducible hernia → **emergency surgery**
**Water-soluble contrast (Gastrografin) challenge**: AXR at 8–24 h
Contrast in colon → resolves · no resolution by **72 h → surgery** (laparoscopic adhesiolysis if feasible)
Right → resection + anastomosis · left → resection, Hartmann’s or **stent as bridge**; caecum > 12 cm = perforation risk
**Flexible sigmoidoscopic decompression** + flatus tube
Elective sigmoid colectomy (high recurrence) · gangrene → Hartmann’s · caecal volvulus → right hemicolectomy

nodes.t: Pseudo-obstruction (Ogilvie): no mechanical cause → correct electrolytes, stop opioids; **neostigmine** or colonoscopic decompression
Left iliac fossa pain, fever, raised CRP
**CT with IV contrast** to confirm and grade (modified Hinchey)

n.t: Immunocompetent, well → analgesia, oral fluids, **antibiotics not routinely needed**; outpatient
IV antibiotics; **abscess ≥ 4–5 cm → CT-guided percutaneous drainage**
Laparoscopic resection with **primary anastomosis ± defunctioning ileostomy**; Hartmann’s if unstable · lavage in selected
Resuscitate → **Hartmann’s procedure** (damage control if septic shock)

nodes.t: **Colonoscopy / CT colonography ~6 weeks** after a complicated episode to exclude cancer
Elective resection case by case (not by number of attacks): fistula (colovesical → pneumaturia), stricture, persistent symptoms, immunosuppressed

intest.title: Acute severe ulcerative colitis (and surgery in IBD)

nodes.t: Bloody diarrhoea ≥ 6/day + one of: HR > 90, T > 37.8 °C, Hb < 105 g/L, ESR > 30 (Truelove & Witts)
Admit (joint medical–surgical care): stool culture + **C. difficile**, CRP, albumin, AXR (colon > 5.5 cm = toxic megacolon), flexible sigmoidoscopy
**IV hydrocortisone 100 mg qds** (or methylprednisolone 60 mg/day), IV fluids, K⁺, **LMWH**; avoid opioids, antidiarrhoeals, NSAIDs

n.t: Switch to oral prednisolone taper + maintenance (thiopurine/biologic)
**Rescue: infliximab or ciclosporin**
No response by day 5–7 → surgery
**Emergency subtotal colectomy + end ileostomy**

nodes.t: Later: **ileal pouch–anal anastomosis** or proctectomy · Crohn’s: bowel-sparing — ileocaecal resection, strictureplasty; drain abscess before anti-TNF
Severe pain on defecation lasting hours + bright red blood on paper
Gentle parting of buttocks: **posterior midline tear** (± sentinel tag); avoid PR/proctoscopy if too painful
Atypical (lateral, multiple, painless, large) → **EUA + biopsy**: Crohn’s, HIV, TB, syphilis, SCC
**Fibre, fluids, laxatives, warm baths, topical lidocaine** — most acute fissures heal
Chronic (> 6 weeks) → **topical diltiazem 2% or GTN 0.4%** for 6–8 weeks (GTN headache)

n.t: **Lateral internal sphincterotomy** (> 90% heal; small risk of incontinence)
**Botulinum toxin** ± fissurectomy · advancement flap; avoid sphincterotomy

nodes.t: Children: constipation management is the key
Painless bright red bleeding on the pan ± prolapsing lump, pruritus
PR + proctoscopy; **exclude colorectal cancer**: FIT / colonoscopy if ≥ 50, change in bowel habit, iron deficiency
All: **fibre, fluids, avoid straining**; topical agents for symptoms

e.g. 0.18% NaCl/4% glucose + KCl; 20–25 mL/kg/day if elderly, frail, renal/cardiac failure
Add measured ongoing losses (vomiting, NG, fistula, drains, third space) with matched electrolyte content

nodes.t: **Reassess**: daily U&E, fluid balance, weight; stop IV fluids as soon as possible
Excess 0.9% saline → **hyperchloraemic acidosis**; hypotonic fluids → **hyponatraemia** (dangerous in children)
Abnormal U&E in a surgical patient — repeat if unexpected (haemolysis), ECG, review fluids and drugs

n.t: **IV calcium** (30 mL 10% gluconate or 10 mL 10% chloride) to protect the heart
**Insulin 10 units + 25 g glucose** IV; salbutamol 10–20 mg nebulised
Remove K⁺: stop culprit drugs, sodium zirconium cyclosilicate, **dialysis if refractory**; monitor glucose
Assess volume status, serum/urine osmolality, urine Na (SIADH common post-op)
Severe symptoms (seizure, coma) → **150 mL 3% saline over 20 min**, repeat until Na ↑ 5 mmol/L
**Limit rise to ≤ 10 mmol/L in 24 h** (osmotic demyelination) · hypovolaemic → 0.9% saline · SIADH → fluid restriction
IV KCl **≤ 10 mmol/h peripherally** (higher only centrally with ECG monitoring); correct **magnesium**; oral if 3.0–3.4

nodes.t: Hypokalaemia → **paralytic ileus** and arrhythmias · never give potassium as a bolus

metab.title: Metabolic response to surgery and nutritional support
metab.source: NICE CG32 · ESPEN 2021 Clinical Nutrition in Surgery · ERAS Society

nodes.t: Injury/surgery → **ebb phase** (hours: ↓ metabolic rate) → **flow phase** (days: catabolism, then anabolism)
Cortisol, catecholamines, glucagon, ADH, aldosterone, IL-6 → hyperglycaemia, protein breakdown, Na/water retention
Blunt it with **ERAS**: clear fluids to 2 h pre-op, carbohydrate loading, regional analgesia, early oral feeding
**MUST** screen: BMI < 18.5, unintentional weight loss > 10% in 3–6 months, or little intake > 5 days → nutrition support

nodes.q: Is the gut working and accessible?

n.t: **Enteral**: oral supplements → NG/NJ tube → gastrostomy/jejunostomy if > 4 weeks
**Parenteral nutrition** via PICC/central line; watch line sepsis, LFTs, glucose

nodes.t: **Refeeding risk** → start ≤ 10 kcal/kg/day (5 if extreme), thiamine before feeding, daily PO₄, K, Mg
Severely malnourished elective patients: **7–14 days pre-op nutrition** before major surgery

shock.title: Undifferentiated shock
shock.source: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 · NICE NG51 · RCUK Anaphylaxis 2021

nodes.t: Hypotension, tachycardia, ↓ urine output, confusion, **lactate > 2 mmol/L**
ABCDE, high-flow O₂, 2 large-bore cannulae, bloods incl. lactate, crossmatch, cultures; catheter for hourly UO
Bedside **echo/POCUS** + JVP + skin: classify the shock

n.t: **Stop the bleeding**, blood products, see haemorrhage chart
Sepsis: **antibiotics within 1 h**, 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloid, source control · anaphylaxis: **IM adrenaline 500 µg**, repeat at 5 min
ECG/troponin → PCI for ACS; **dobutamine** ± noradrenaline; avoid fluid overload
**Decompress** tension pneumothorax, drain tamponade, thrombolyse massive PE

nodes.t: Persistent hypotension → **noradrenaline** to **MAP ≥ 65 mmHg**; add vasopressin ± hydrocortisone in septic shock
Neurogenic (spinal injury above T6: hypotension + bradycardia) → fluids, noradrenaline, atropine · adrenal crisis → **hydrocortisone 100 mg IV**

shock.title: Haemorrhagic shock and major haemorrhage
shock.source: ATLS 10th ed · BSH/JPAC Major Haemorrhage · ESA/European Trauma 2023

nodes.t: Bleeding patient with signs of shock
Estimate loss — **ATLS class**: I < 15% · II 15–30% (tachycardia) · III 31–40% (hypotension) · IV > 40%
**Control the source** (pressure, tourniquet, binder) and **activate major haemorrhage protocol**
**TXA 1 g over 10 min within 3 h**, then 1 g over 8 h
**Balanced blood products** (RBC:FFP 1:1, add platelets and cryoprecipitate); minimise crystalloid; warmed fluids, check ionised Ca²⁺
**Permissive hypotension** (SBP 80–90 mmHg) until bleeding controlled — not in TBI (keep MAP ≥ 80)

n.t: Observe; CT to define injuries
**Damage-control surgery** or interventional radiology now

nodes.t: Targets: Hb 70–90 g/L, platelets > 75 × 10⁹/L (> 100 in TBI), **fibrinogen > 1.5 g/L**, PT ratio < 1.5; viscoelastic testing
Avoid the **lethal triad**: hypothermia, acidosis, coagulopathy (+ hypocalcaemia)
Surgical patient who may need blood
Pre-op: correct anaemia (IV iron); **TXA if expected blood loss > 500 mL**; cell salvage
**Restrictive threshold Hb 70 g/L** (target 70–90); 80 g/L if ACS; give **single units** and reassess if not bleeding
Bedside **positive patient ID**, observations before, 15 min after start and at end

nodes.q: Acute reaction — stop transfusion, check ID

br.l: Fever, loin pain, hypotension, red urine

n.t: **ABO incompatibility**: stop, resuscitate, return unit, DAT, haemolysis screen, watch for DIC/AKI
**Anaphylaxis**: IM adrenaline 500 µg, fluids
**TRALI** (bilateral infiltrates, normal JVP) → O₂/ventilation · **TACO** (overload, ↑ BP) → diuretic
Febrile non-haemolytic: paracetamol, restart slowly

nodes.t: Report serious reactions to **SHOT / MHRA SABRE**

obesity.title: Selection and work-up for bariatric surgery

nodes.t: Adult with obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²)
Exclude secondary causes when suggested clinically: **TSH**, cortisol (Cushing’s), drugs; screen for eating disorders
Specialist weight management: diet, activity, behavioural; **GLP-1/GIP agonists** (semaglutide, tirzepatide)

n.t: Refer for **bariatric surgery** if fit and committed to lifelong follow-up
**Expedited assessment** (metabolic surgery); thresholds 2.5 lower for Asian/Black ethnicity

nodes.t: Pre-op: OSA screening (STOP-BANG/CPAP), smoking cessation, nutritional bloods, selective OGD, **2-week liver-shrinking diet**
Procedure: **sleeve gastrectomy** (commonest) · **Roux-en-Y gastric bypass** (preferred with GORD/T2DM) · OAGB · SADI-S/duodenal switch for super-obesity
Lifelong: multivitamin, calcium + vit D, iron, **IM B₁₂ 3-monthly**, annual bloods · avoid pregnancy for 12–18 months
Bariatric patient unwell after surgery

n.t: **Leak**: persistent **tachycardia > 120** may be the only sign → CT with oral + IV contrast
Unstable → **re-laparoscopy**, washout, drains · contained → drainage + endoscopic stent/vacuum
Also: bleeding, PE (extended prophylaxis), gastric outlet narrowing after sleeve
**Internal hernia** (Petersen’s): CT mesenteric swirl
**Diagnostic laparoscopy even if CT normal** — risk of bowel infarction
Marginal ulcer (smoking, NSAIDs) → PPI · anastomotic stricture → endoscopic dilatation
**Dumping**: early (osmotic, 30 min) / late (hypoglycaemia, 1–3 h) → small meals, avoid simple sugars
Gallstones (UDCA × 6 months) · band slip/erosion → deflate/remove · deficiencies (iron, B₁₂, folate)

nodes.t: Persistent vomiting → give **thiamine before glucose** (Wernicke’s encephalopathy)
